commander_identity.mechanical_plan: Cast Admiral Beckett Brass for {1}{U}{B}{R}; connect with three different Pirates against the same opponent, then use Admiral's beginning-endstep ability to gain control of an eligible nonland permanent. Repeat through cheap evasive Pirates, recurring blocker disruption and on-hit draw/treasure.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Power Bracket 4 — Optimized: persistent multiplayer permanent theft and combat-value Pirate swarm, with interaction, tutors and valuable back-up combat damage. Requires three distinct combat connections, stable commander and legal endstep targets; not forced into generic cEDH.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Retain Pirates, evasion, recurring Daring Piracy entries, Merchant Raiders lockdown, The Indomitable combat draw, Open into Wonder card flow and stolen-permanent synergies; avoid replacing unique theft identity with unrelated Grixis goodstuff or noncombat storm.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: Whole 99-card role audit in Admiral opportunity and deep reviews: 35 lands, 34 creatures (33 Pirate/changeling bodies), one-drop evasive enablers, Pirate-entry/trade effects, Malcolm/Breeches/Ramirez loot and Treasures, Kindred Discovery/Bident/Indomitable on-hit draw, Vampiric/Demonic tutoring, Daring Piracy token pressure, Merchant Raiders evasion lock, sweep-resistant recovery and theft payoffs. Cuts must preserve three distinct combat connections rather than simply buff power.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: Exact D still has 35 lands with Island 3, Mountain 2, Swamp 1 and 3 typed fetch lands. City replaces always-tapped Crumbling and triggers one self-damage when tapped, improving a demonstrated four-land Admiral casting line. Creature mana-value distribution including Admiral is 6/8/7/8/5 across MV1–MV5 versus baseline 5/9/7/8/5; typed fetch, tribal-restricted colored sources, conditional taplands and two-blue Open X=3 costs all accounted for.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Toxic Deluge, Chaos Warp, Cyclonic Rift, Fierce Guardianship, Deflecting Swat, Counterspell/Mana Drain and Pirate tribal protection interact with attackers and board; Merchant Raiders and Open clear blocks, Indomitable/Bident/Discovery replenish hits, March of the Drowned and Admiral Brass support recovery. Flyers/reach/Spirits, Fog, spot removal, timing, City self-damage and paid Broadside boast are tested adverse limitations, not assumed away.

weakest_slots.weakness: A guaranteed-tapped three-color land postpones four-mana Admiral when drawn as the fourth source; its painless fixing can still be useful in a slow game.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Swap an always-tapped source for immediate UBR access while transparently accepting City's every-tap triggered self-damage.

weakest_slots.weakness: Pirate's recurring evasion requires 2U each combat and can conflict with casting and protecting the commander, although combat loot is genuine.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Deckhand is already hard to block against non-Spirits for the same printed {1}{U} and pays for another creature only when needed; removal-spell targeting is a downside.

weakest_slots.weakness: Ground-based attacker scales power when other Pirates attack but does not secure the third distinct hit that Beckett counts.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Move a source into the first-turn flying slot; losing ground defense and attack-scaling damage is a deliberate commander-first tradeoff.

weakest_slots.weakness: Flash deathtouch gives useful instant-speed trading and attacking-Pirate combat trick but does not inherently evade blockers as a third source.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Skyship flies over ground blockers and adds existing counters on a hit, including a verified conditional Malcolm chorus line; weaker against flyers and reach.

weakest_slots.weakness: Three-mana topdeck Pirate tutor and repeated noncombat each-opponent Pirate-entry drain are valuable but do not themselves produce a same-player three-Pirate hit.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Haste/menace yields immediate attacking Pirate pressure and paid postattack removal; forfeits true tutor/attrition capacity, especially repeated Daring Piracy tokens.

weakest_slots.weakness: Four-mana body delays immediate offense and may die to removal; competing Blustersquall can tap every opposing creature at instant speed once.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain Raiders for repeating Pirate-entry tap that keeps blockers frozen while it survives; a one-turn all-blocker tap gives up core permanent-theft support.

weakest_slots.weakness: Four-mana non-Pirate Vehicle competes with developing early Pirates and can be stranded when behind on board.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain this uncrewed passive per-combat-hit draw engine and conditional graveyard reuse; replacing it with one-shot tap sacrifices game-long card access.

weakest_slots.weakness: An XUU sorcery consumes five mana and two blue to unblock three creatures, exposing it to reactive spells and mana bottlenecks.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain guaranteed unblockable targeting and actual on-hit draw when X=3; War Cadence is a paid repeated tax opponents may pay and removes the card reward.

weakest_slots.weakness: Cheap recursion can be small after a multi-creature wipe and may be a narrow late topdeck.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain the flexible one-Pirate or two-Pirate recovery in a mixed table rather than a five-mana symmetrical tribal rebirth that often aids opponents.

weakest_slots.weakness: Five-mana creature temporarily borrows a hand creature rather than directly guaranteeing a Pirate damage source; attack timing is fragile.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Retain repeatable Pirate-themed temporary opposing-hand theft; Kindred Charge is six mana, needs an already-wide board, and loses legendary copies to legend rule.

weakest_slots.weakness: Expensive legend consumes upper curve and is weak when the graveyard has few Pirates.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Keep actual Pirate recovery and named Admiral identity rather than a symmetrical burst of exile-bound copies that cannot fix an empty board.

weakest_slots.weakness: Always enters tapped and can delay an on-curve four-mana commander despite future Pirate-cast scry.
weakest_slots.reasoning: Keep UBR commander-colored production and on-type scry; colorless Access Tunnel plus three-mana activation is too expensive for a deck already demanding UBR.

whole_deck_audit.current_baseline_strength: The locked approved Pirate list is a coherent optimized theft deck, with Forerunner tutoring and each-opponent entry drain, Poisoner flash and deathtouch, Captain scaling damage, Saboteur loot, strong blue combat draw and three signature Raider/Indomitable/Open engines; those benefits were not mislabeled as weak simply because five challengers exist.
whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: M5 ranked pool, prior 62 source-linked deep reviews, owner-equivalent Pass C, EDHREC commander/Pirate/unblockable leads, complete 99-card slot audit, 24 current Oracle-checked material candidates, at least 12 incumbent challenges, exact canonical baseline plus fully specified 100-card A/B/C/D packages. No new broad research pipeline run was necessary.
whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: OFF-RANKING Pirate evasion and utility cards were examined alongside EDHREC-ranked themes: Cloud Pirates, Departed Deckhand, Skyship Plunderer, Broadside Bombardiers, Forerunner, ascend Scoundrel, global Blustersquall, War Cadence, tribal Horn, Neckbreaker and Kindred Charge. D wins with protected repeating theft/draw rather than unexamined off-ranking options.

D's verified payable early evasive line and preserved repeat engines attack that failure mode directly.
